Hankook Tire & Technology Co Ltd Emerges from Insolvency, Resumes Operations

Hankook Tire & Technology Co Ltd, one of South Korea’s largest automotive suppliers, has successfully emerged from insolvency proceedings, the company confirmed this week. After a turbulent period marked by financial uncertainty, operations at Hankook’s major manufacturing plants have now resumed, alleviating concerns among industry partners and employees.

The company, a leading producer of tires for both domestic and international automakers, entered court-led administration in late March following prolonged cash flow problems and mounting debt obligations. According to a statement from Hankook’s interim management, decisive restructuring measures and an agreement with creditors paved the way for the court’s approval to lift insolvency restrictions late last week.

“Thanks to the dedication of our workforce and the support from our stakeholders, we have stabilized the business and are looking forward to restoring full production capacity,” said Lee Hyun-woo, Chief Restructuring Officer, at a press briefing on Tuesday. “We are committed to regaining the trust of our partners and customers.”

Union representatives at the Daejeon and Geumsan plants said operations restarted in recent days, with most employees returning to their posts. “There was real anxiety about jobs, but the restart is a relief,” said Kim Min-jun, a spokesperson for the Hankook Workers’ Union. “We hope management keeps its promises on investment and job security.”

Industry analysts say the resumption of production at Hankook is vital for South Korea’s automotive sector. “Hankook supplies a significant share of OE and replacement tires domestically and exports to over 180 countries,” noted Park Ji-hoon, analyst at Seoul-based Hanseong Research. “Any prolonged disruption would have put further strain on vehicle makers and the broader auto supply chain.”

The Korea Automotive Industry Association welcomed the resolution, citing the importance of Hankook’s operations to the sector’s stability. Going forward, the company says it will focus on operational efficiency and financial discipline as it seeks to rebuild market confidence and maintain its position as a key supplier to the global automotive industry.
